thessaloniki.deliverable: D5.2, SPICE Masterplan for the Municipality of Thessaloniki, due at M34
thessaloniki.expectedResult: A detailed master plan for the requalification of a green public space, transforming it into a model associated with a dedicated sports park.

sections.title: Spatial characteristics
bullets: The park has a radial spatial layout.
It is surrounded by important local services.
Only approximately one-third of the park is intensively used, mainly the playground, pergola and amphitheatre.
Directional and tactile signage for people with disabilities is discontinuous.
Localised flooding occurs in some areas.

sections.title: Suggested interventions
bullets: Plan the park together with its immediate surroundings rather than treating it as an isolated site.
Prioritise smaller, targeted interventions instead of major radical changes.
Cooperate with the "Friends of the Park" group and local businesses on short-term projects.
Connect the neighbouring pocket garden to the main park.
Create links with the other SPICE cities.
Involve local people in technical and maintenance activities.

participationInsights.title: Credible participation
participationInsights.text: Participation must feel meaningful, with a clear influence on decisions and visible results.

participationInsights.title: Long-term stewardship
participationInsights.text: Future care should not depend exclusively on municipal maintenance. Responsibility should be shared with local allies, volunteers and stewardship groups.

participationInsights.title: A shared definition of care
participationInsights.text: Maintenance includes both technical responsibility and everyday practices such as cleaning, gardening, repainting, repairing and preventing neglect.

participationInsights.title: Specific engagement profiles
participationInsights.text: Groups requiring dedicated attention include older people, children and adolescents, people with disabilities, dog owners, and shop owners.

participationInsights.title: Mediation between different needs
participationInsights.text: Different groups may have conflicting expectations, so co-design must include negotiation and prioritisation.

participationInsights.title: Education as an activation strategy
participationInsights.text: Schools and educational initiatives can help build trust, responsibility and long-term engagement.

additionalNotes.title: Additional ideas recorded during the workshop
bullets: More space for children to run and play football.
Improved safety around children’s areas, including consideration of fencing.
Spaces suitable for several different user groups.
Designated green and recreational areas.
Gathering spaces, kiosks and urban furniture.
Clearer zoning of activities.
Making the park a place for gathering, relaxing, picnicking and informal social use.

bielsko-biala.deliverable: D5.3, SPICE Masterplan for ARRSA, due at M34
bielsko-biala.expectedResult: A detailed master plan for the street and its surrounding urban context.

sections.title: Spatial and historical characteristics
bullets: The street is Bielsko-Biała’s main pedestrian axis.
It acts as a structural spine connecting areas that once belonged to the formerly separate cities of Bielsko and Biała.
It remains an important part of the city centre’s public life.
It is predominantly car-free and functions as a soft-mobility corridor for pedestrians and cyclists.
It connects important civic and cultural destinations.

sections.title: Heritage value
bullets: Several officially protected buildings.
Preserved cobbled paving.
Period-style street lighting.
A strong historic townscape character.
A cultural trail connecting City Hall, monumental squares and remnants of historic fortifications.

sections.title: Environmental and public-space potential
bullets: Additional greenery.
Improved public seating.
Ecological improvements.
Better pedestrian comfort.
Stronger active-travel connections.

sections.title: Economic and urban challenges
bullets: The street has lost some of its former commercial vitality.
Footfall and retail activity have declined.
There are increasing numbers of vacant commercial premises and empty shopfronts.
Small independent businesses are under pressure.
The street competes with the nearby Sfera Shopping Center and other large-scale retail developments.
The broader context is one of declining high-street trade, despite the street’s central historical and cultural role.

participationInsights.title: Trust and communication
participationInsights.text: Previous participation processes had low turnout and resulted in limited implementation.

participationInsights.title: Sensitive adaptation
participationInsights.text: Changes must respect the historic character while addressing accessibility, greenery, weather protection and the reduction of car presence.

participationInsights.title: Targeted communication
participationInsights.text: Storytelling, social media and direct one-to-one engagement are needed, particularly to reach less-active groups.

participationInsights.title: Entrepreneurs as a priority group
participationInsights.text: Former, current and potential entrepreneurs are central actors and require direct dialogue and specific incentives.

additionalNotes.title: Direction for the next phase
bullets: Move from problem framing towards a new shared vision for the street.

cuba.deliverable: D5.4, SPICE Masterplan for the Municipality of Cuba, due at M34
cuba.expectedResult: A detailed master plan for the requalification and reactivation of the site.

sections.title: Location and significance
bullets: The fountain occupies a key position at the town entrance.
It is easily accessible and well connected to the town centre.
It has strong emotional and community significance, especially for older residents.
Its tangible value comes from its vernacular architecture.
Its intangible value comes from its history as a lively community gathering place.

sections.title: Current condition
bullets: The site is closed and disused.
It has lost its former social function.
Continued disuse creates a risk of physical deterioration.
The surrounding area is still used informally by school students and by communities that do not live immediately nearby.
It is perceived as unsafe and poorly maintained.

sections.title: Water and infrastructure issues
bullets: Seasonal flooding occurs from approximately October to April.
The site contains rainwater-collection or tank infrastructure.
Sewage overflow and mixed sewage points are identified as problems.

sections.title: Social and design priorities — climate-responsive comfort
paragraphs: The renewed site should be sustainable, green, inclusive, responsive to climatic conditions, and capable of serving different user needs.

sections.title: Visible and practical results
paragraphs: The process must deliver concrete, visible and implementable changes rather than remaining theoretical.

sections.title: Community appropriation and long-term use
paragraphs: The objective is not only to consult residents. The community should gradually take ownership of the space and help keep it active and relevant.

participationInsights.title: Young people
participationInsights.text: Engagement must consider recognition, accessibility, language, belonging and cultural identity.

participationInsights.title: Older people
participationInsights.text: Engagement must consider recognition, accessibility, language, belonging and cultural identity.

participationInsights.title: Migrants
participationInsights.text: Engagement must consider recognition, accessibility, language, belonging and cultural identity.

rovaniemi.deliverable: D5.5, SPICE Masterplan for RoMa, due at M34
rovaniemi.expectedResult: A detailed master plan for the adaptive reuse and wider integration of the bus-station site.

sections.title: Strategic role and physical character
bullets: The station is one of the principal entry points or "portals" to the city.
Its interior has a distinctive modernist architectural character.
The indoor spaces could support new programmes and uses, provided heritage constraints are respected.
Some outdoor areas are currently used for snow storage.

sections.title: Principal challenges — uncertain future function
paragraphs: A viable new use must be identified that balances heritage protection, contemporary community needs, mobility requirements, and the building’s potential for public and social use.

sections.title: Principal challenges — physical deterioration
bullets: Roof deterioration.
Deterioration of the wood façade.
Water infiltration from the soil.

sections.title: Related planned interventions
bullets: Renovation of the street connecting the station to the city centre is in progress.
An Olympic-size swimming hall is proposed to the south of the site, but remains to be confirmed.
Bus services may be redistributed to the nearby railway station, also subject to confirmation.

participationInsights.title: Trust-based local connections
participationInsights.text: Engagement should use existing trusted relationships and work through established local partners.

participationInsights.title: Youth-led and informal participation
participationInsights.text: Participation should be social, flexible and enjoyable, and should take place closer to the spaces young people already use.

participationInsights.title: Different youth profiles
participationInsights.text: "Youth at risk" should not be treated as one homogeneous group. Teenagers, students and young adults outside education or employment have different needs and vulnerabilities.

participationInsights.title: Autonomy and agency
participationInsights.text: Young people need spaces where they can be visible, act independently and express identity, creativity and purpose.

additionalNotes.title: Context that could change the site’s future
bullets: These surrounding projects (street renovation, swimming hall, possible bus redistribution) could significantly change the role, accessibility and future programme of the bus-station building.

conclusions.timingNote: Slide labels for the demo sites state an implementation period of M18–M34, while the embedded implementation-roadmap graphics state M13–M34; this timing should be clarified. Each site is expected to produce a detailed SPICE master plan at M34, supported by the Demo Action Plan.
bullets: Master planning must lead to visible implementation, not only consultation or theoretical proposals.
Trust is a central issue, especially where previous participation produced limited results.
Engagement must be adapted to specific groups, rather than relying on general public consultations.
Long-term maintenance and stewardship should involve communities, local organisations and businesses.
Accessibility and inclusion are recurring concerns.
Existing identity and heritage must be retained, whether this concerns a historic street, vernacular water infrastructure or modernist architecture.
Climate and environmental resilience appear through flooding, water management, greenery, comfort and seasonal conditions.

perSiteStrategy.strategy: Better distribution of uses, accessibility and community stewardship.
Revitalisation of commercial and public life while protecting historic character.
Reactivation of a closed heritage site while resolving water, maintenance and inclusion issues.
Identification of a viable heritage-compatible use, with a strong emphasis on youth agency and changing mobility conditions.
